title: Implicit Auto-Initialization Assumptions
pattern: Allocating variables (especially locks or control state) on the stack and omitting explicit initialization, expecting the compiler to zero-initialize them.
why_bad: Stack-allocated auto variables in languages like C/C++ are not initialized by default; they contain whatever random garbage was left on the stack, leading to highly unpredictable, non-deterministic bugs.
detection: Declaring local (auto) variables in C/C++ without assigning an initial value or calling an explicit constructor.
counterexample: Always explicitly initializing stack variables: `int lock = 0;`.
fix: Always explicitly initialize local variables at the point of declaration: `int lock = 0;`.
